chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: 'Midnight', 'What a Difference a Day Makes' and her Carter repertoire
summary: Discussion of the songs on the Carter sides and a joke about Dinah Washington.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Of the records you made with Benny Carter one was called "Midnight" which is a song I think that he wrote.
And "What a Difference a Day Made".
Well, "What A Difference A Day Made" was a pop tune.
Possibly you taught Dinah Washington to sing?
No, maybe she heard it. Nobody taught Dinah Washington to sing. Dinah Washington
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
was born with what she has.
Do you remember what else you sang? I presume you sang those two songs, didn't you?

Yeah, and in my repertoire I had "The Things We Did Last Summer" and, I'm really not sure of some of the things. I wouldn't have done anymore than six songs a night. And I didn't go on as a featured singer. I mean, if the band played that arrangement I sang it. Of course, "Loch Lomond" was always the big thing and "Saint Louis Blues".
So some of Benny Carter arrangements of those songs?

No, they were arrangements made I did "Yes, I'm Coming, Virginia" by Benny. / And I enjoyed it and it's only recently that I am, more or less, received as a singer of popular tunes. And even now when I perform they'll holler our "Loch Lomond".

I notice, I have a record at home of some performances from the Benny Carter Band when it was on the west coast and there's a version of "Midnight" on the album that I have with Savannah Churchill. Do you know anything about that?

She's not all that great, I thought.
She recorded that before or after?
This was at least 1944 so it's probably three years after you.
